problem.name: Forrelation
problem.statement_latex: Given phase oracles $f,g:\{0,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$, distinguish the promised large and small values of $\Phi(f,g)=2^{-3n/2}\sum_{x,y}f(x)(-1)^{x\cdot y}g(y)$. The $k$-fold version alternates $k$ phase functions and Hadamard transforms.
problem.statement_text: Given phase oracles $f,g:\{0,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$, distinguish the promised large and small values of $\Phi(f,g)=2^{-3n/2}\sum_{x,y}f(x)(-1)^{x\cdot y}g(y)$. The $k$-fold version alternates $k$ phase functions and Hadamard transforms.

strength.description_latex: Exponential or subexponential to polynomial in the strongest stated regime.

hardware.description_latex: The transform circuit uses $O(n)$ logical qubits and $O(n)$ elementary gates around its oracle calls; implementing the oracle determines the full device cost. Small circuit demonstrations are feasible.

quantum.headline_latex: $O(1)$ queries and $O(n)$ gates for two-function Forrelation; $O(k)$ queries for $k$-fold Forrelation, by Aaronson--Ambainis.
quantum.headline_text: $O(1)$ queries and $O(n)$ gates for two-function Forrelation; $O(k)$ queries for $k$-fold Forrelation, by Aaronson–Ambainis.

classical.headline_latex: $\Omega(2^{n/2}/n)$ randomized queries for the two-function promise, with an $\widetilde O(2^{n/2})$ classical algorithm. These bounds are tight up to logarithmic factors.
